agent_trace.summary: On a head MRI, very dark areas at the top of the image are often structures with little mobile hydrogen signal, most commonly bone or air-filled spaces. In an axial image through the skull base/posterior fossa, the paranasal sinuses and skull base bones can appear black, while the brain tissue, brainstem, and cerebellum are brighter than these voids.

key_facts: On MRI, cortical bone usually appears very dark because it has low signal.
Air in the paranasal sinuses also appears black on MRI due to no signal.
In head images, the 'top' of an axial slice may correspond to anterior skull base/sinus regions depending on orientation.
Normal brain structures like the cerebellum and brainstem should have soft tissue signal, not the very low signal of air or bone.
